SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
S.1, Special Branch 4444,
REPORT
Date July 22, 19 38.

Subject Lights believed to be signals seen in tower of Yangtze
Hotel, Yunnan Road.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford S N

As a result of a report having been received to
the effect that signalling by means of lights was observed
in the tower of the Yangtze Hotel, Yunnan Road, between
1.30 a.m. and 2.43 a.m. July 20, 1938, observation was
kept on the Hotel by a member of the Special Branch
posted in the Woo Kong Hotel, corner of Foochow and Fokien
Roads, on the night of July 21/22, 1938, but nothing
suspicious was seen. Special Branch detectives visited
the Yangtze Hotel at 11.30 a.m. July 22, 1938, but
failed to find anything that would indicate that signalling
was being done from the roof garden or the tower. In
the course of an examination of the premises, it was
observed that an electric light bulb, set on top of the
elevator engine located in the tower aforesaid, showed
a light every time the elevator was in motion and became
extinguished as soon as the elevator stopped and also
when the latter was passing the different floors. This
light would appear to be the explanation of what was
suspected to be signalling. The light is an indicator
to the engine attendant that the elevator is functioning.
Windows in the engine room face due East and due South.
It was explained by the manager of the Hotel that he had
painted the windows of the room in question shortly after
August 13, 1937, but that with the advent of the hot
weather the windows were recently thrown open.

S.1，特务科 4444，
报告
日期 1938年7月22日。

事由 据信云南路扬子饭店塔楼内出现的灯光是信号。

制作人 警司 Logan 转呈人 C. Crawford S N

鉴于收到一份报告，称在1938年7月20日凌晨1时30分至2时43分之间，观察到有人利用灯光在云南路扬子饭店的塔楼内进行信号联络，特务科一名成员于1938年7月21/22日晚在福州路与福建路交界处的吴宫酒店（Woo Kong Hotel）对扬子饭店进行了监视，但未发现任何可疑情况。特务科侦探于1938年7月22日上午11时30分走访了扬子饭店，但未能发现任何迹象表明有人从屋顶花园或塔楼发出信号。在检查场所的过程中，观察到安装在上述塔楼内电梯发动机顶部的一只电灯泡，每当电梯运行时就会亮起，一旦电梯停止以及在经过不同楼层时就会熄灭。这盏灯似乎就是被怀疑为信号联络现象的解释。该灯光向发动机操作员指示电梯正在运行。发动机室的窗户分别朝向正东和正南。饭店经理解释说，他在1937年8月13日之后不久就粉刷了相关房间的窗户，但随着炎热天气的到来，最近窗户被敞开了。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............ 8039 A
S.I. Special Branch/6/4/6/6 35
REPORT
Date June 7, 19 38
Subject Mysterious lights reported seen from 7th floor of Sun Company
Building, Nanking Road.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Gaspard
On 1.6.38. information was received from Mr. V.H.
Bourne, Deputy Treasurer-Revenue, Shanghai Municipal Council,
to the effect that while he was sitting on the verandah of
the Race Club between 7.15 p.m. and 8 p.m., 31.5.38, he
observed what appeared to be signalling by lights from the
7th floor of the Sun Company Building, Nanking Road near
Lloyd Road. The lights, which appeared to be flashed off
and on as in Morse Code, were observed coming from the 4th
and 1st window from Lloyd Road. As the 7th floor of the
Sun Company Building faces Lootun, Mr. Bourne suspected
that some person was communicating with mobile units in
that area.
Observation was kept on the building nightly from
June 1st to June 5th by members of the Special Branch, but
nothing suspicious was seen.
The floor in question is used as an amusement resort,
being part of the Roof Garden, therefore it does not appear
likely that such a public place would be chosen as a place
from which to signal by means of lights.
As a matter of courtesy, Mr. Bourne was informed
of the result of enquiries.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE * JUNE 1938 * SPECIAL BRANCH）

档案号............ 8039 A
S.I. 特务科/6/4/6/6 35
报告
日期 1938年6月7日
事由 据报南京路先施公司大楼七层出现神秘灯光。
制作人 警司 Logan 转呈人 C. Gaspard
1938年6月1日，收到上海公共租界工部局副总会计师兼税务局副局长 V.H. Bourne 先生的信息，称他在1938年5月31日晚上7时15分至8时之间坐在跑马总会（Race Club）的阳台上时，观察到南京路靠近 Lloyd Road（音译）的先施公司大楼七层似乎有灯光信号。这些灯光看起来像摩尔斯电码一样闪烁，据观察是从靠近 Lloyd Road（音译）的第4扇和第1扇窗户发出的。由于先施公司大楼的七层面向 Lootun（音译），Bourne 先生怀疑有人在与该区域的移动部队进行联络。
特务科成员从6月1日至6月5日每晚对该大楼进行监视，但未发现任何可疑情况。
涉事楼层作为游乐场所使用，是屋顶花园的一部分，因此不太可能选择这样一个公共场所作为灯光信号的发射点。
出于礼貌，已将调查结果通知 Bourne 先生。
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 * 1938年6月 * 特务科）

PARK HOTEL

Shanghai, October 16, 1937.

The Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:

With reference to the allegations made by the Japanese spokesman and published in the Press to-day, stating that the roof of the Park Hotel is being used as an observation post by Chinese officers, we beg to inform you that the top of our building is being occupied by the U.S. Marine Corps as an observation post; application to install this post was made by Captain R.A. Boone, Brigade Intelligence Office together with an Inspector of the Municipal Police. No one except marine and naval personnel is admitted.

We also wish to emphasize that no unauthorized person is permitted to loiter in any part of our building and that we gladly submit to inspections of the Shanghai Municipal Police at any time and without notice.

With a view to prevent any misunderstanding, we would greatly appreciate if you could kindly notify both the Chinese and Japanese military authorities, of the above.

Thanking you, we are,

Yours faithfully,

MAX SCHIBLER,

Manager.

国际饭店

上海，1937年10月16日。

秘书，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海。

尊敬的先生：

关于日本发言人今日在媒体上发表的指控，称国际饭店屋顶正被中国军官用作观察哨，我们谨告知您，我方大楼顶部正被美国海军陆战队用作观察哨；设立该观察哨的申请是由旅团情报官 R.A. Boone 上尉会同一名工部局警务处督察提出的。除海军陆战队和海军人员外，任何人不得进入。

我们还要强调，不允许任何未经授权的人员在我方大楼的任何部分逗留，并且我们乐意随时接受上海公共租界工部局警务处的突击检查。

为了防止任何误解，如果您能 kindly 将上述情况通知中国和日本军事当局，我们将不胜感激。

谢谢，此致，

您忠实的，

MAX SCHIBLER，

经理。

With reference to the endorsement by the Deputy
Commissioner (Special Branch) on the attached excerpts from
the Shanghai Times dated October 17, 1937, I have to report
that no signalling has been observed from the Park Hotel
during the past few weeks. Inspector Perkins, Officer i/c
Sinza Station stated that the Foreign Y.M.C.A., Park Hotel,
Bubbling Well Road, and the Sun Company, Yu Ya Ching Road,
were under continual observation by detectives and uniform
staff. In addition the American Authorities have taken
adequate measures to counteract any method of visual signalling.

incidents the matter will be made the subject of a report.

SHANGHAI TIMES - 16.10.37.

Park Hotel
Roof Held
By Marines

Alleged Use By Chinese
As Observation Post
Officially Denied

Allegations that the Park Hotel,
Shanghai's 22-storey pile on Bub-
bling Well Road, is being used by
Chinese as an artillery observation
post were made at the press con-
ference yesterday by the Japanese
Naval spokesman.

"The Japanese authorities are in
possession of definite information to
the effect that observers high up in
the Park Hotel building were in
communication with the Chinese
batteries in Chapei during the bar-
rage on Thursday evening," declar-
ed the spokesman.

The Japanese authorities had ex-
pected the S.M.C. to take such steps
as would be necessary to prevent
the use of buildings within the
Settlement for such purposes, the
Japanese continued, and the atten-
tion of the Shanghai Municipal
Council would be drawn to the
matter.

Interviewed last night, Captain
Boone, United States Marine Corps,
described the Japanese allegation
as untrue inasmuch as the Amer-
ican Marines were using the roof
of the Park Hotel as an observation
post, and permission for access to
the roof was refused to all but ac-
credited personnel. This rule, he
said, was strictly adhered to.

A denial also was issued by the
Chinese official spokesman last
night.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月16日。

国际饭店
屋顶由
海军陆战队占据

官方否认
被中国人
用作观察哨的指控

日本海军发言人在昨天的新闻发布会上声称，位于静安寺路的上海22层高楼国际饭店正被中国人用作炮兵观察哨。

发言人宣称：“日本当局掌握确切信息，表明在周四晚上的炮击期间，位于国际饭店高处的观察员与闸北的中国炮兵阵地进行了联络。”

日本人继续说道，日本当局原本期望上海公共租界工部局采取必要措施，防止租界内的建筑物被用于此类目的，并将提请上海公共租界工部局注意此事。

美国海军陆战队 Boone 上尉昨晚在接受采访时称，日本的指控是不实的，因为美国海军陆战队正在使用国际饭店的屋顶作为观察哨，并且除了经认证的人员外，拒绝所有人进入屋顶。他说，这一规定得到了严格遵守。

中国官方发言人昨晚也发表了否认声明。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No.
    .ol, Special Branch    Station,
                REPORT
                        Date. October 14    1937
Subject    Observation Post on the roof of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha
           building located at No. 5, The Bund.
Made by    D.S. Leroy        Forwarded by    C. [Signature] A. S.

    Further to the attached reports from Central Station
dated October 12 and 13 respectively, regarding the
utilization by Japanese Naval Officers of the roof of the
Nisshin Kisen Kaisha building for purposes of observation,
enquiries by members of the Special Branch indicate that the
information contained in the Shanghai Evening Post and
Mercury of October 12 (Vide attached newspaper cutting) is
substantially correct.
    On October 14, when questioned by Special Branch
detectives in the presence of Mr. W.B.O. Middleton, a
director of Burkill and Sons, Ltd. whose offices are
located in the N.K.K. building, Sung Ah-kong (孫阿根),
operator of one of the elevators in the aforementioned
premises, stated that on Saturday, October 9, between 9 a.m.
and 10 a.m., eight or nine Japanese wearing mustard coloured
uniforms arrived in two motor cars at the N.K.K. building
and in the company of the chief of the Import Department
of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha proceeded to the roof of the
building where they remained for a period of about twenty
minutes.    One of the observation party was carrying a
large and powerful pair of binoculars.
    Sung Ah-kong further stated that members of the shore
and floating staff of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha frequently
visited the roof for the express purpose of observation,
particularly during the late afternoon and evening.
    The above information was confirmed by Mr. J.L. Mears
of Thomson and Company whose offices are also located in
the N.K.K. building at the Canton Road entrance of which
two Sikh Police Constables are at present posted.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    档案号
    .ol, 特务科    捕房，
                报告
                        日期. 1937年10月14日
事由    位于外滩5号的日清汽船株式会社大楼屋顶的观察哨。
制作人    副警司 Leroy        转呈人    C. [签名] A. S.

继中央捕房分别于10月12日和13日提交的关于日本海军军官利用日清汽船株式会社大楼屋顶进行观察的报告后，特务科成员的调查显示，《上海晚邮报及信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）10月12日报道中所载信息基本属实（见附报纸剪报）。
10月14日，在 Burkill and Sons, Ltd.（其办公室位于日清汽船株式会社大楼内）董事 W.B.O. Middleton 先生在场的情况下，特务科侦探询问了上述场所的一名电梯操作员孙阿根（Sung Ah-kong）。孙阿根表示，10月9日星期六上午9时至10时之间，八到九名身穿芥末色制服的日本人乘坐两辆汽车到达日清汽船株式会社大楼，并在日清汽船株式会社进口部经理的陪同下前往大楼屋顶，在那里停留了约二十分钟。观察团成员中的一人携带了一副大型高倍望远镜。
孙阿根还指出，日清汽船株式会社的岸上和浮动工作人员经常为了观察目的特意前往屋顶，特别是在下午晚些时候和晚上。
上述信息得到了 Thomson and Company 的 J.L. Mears 先生的证实，该公司的办公室也位于日清汽船株式会社大楼内，其广东路入口处目前驻有两名锡克族巡捕。

In view of the possibility of further visits to the
roof being made by Japanese Naval or Military officers, and
by members of the staff of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, the
liftman, Sung Ah-kong, was instructed that in the event of
his conducting any persons to the roof he was to inform
Mr. Middleton who would immediately inform the Special Branch.
It is of interest to note that an uninterrupted view
of the roof of the N.K.K. building may be obtained from the
top of the Robert Dollar building, 51, Canton Road. In this
connection, Mr. Middleton expressed the opinion that
Mr. H.B. Gibson of the Robert Dollar Company would be only
too pleased to arrange for the Municipal Police to be granted
all facilities for conducting any observation which might be
considered necessary. A fairly comprehensive view of the
roof of the N.K.K. building may also be obtained from the
Police observation post.

D.J. (Special Branch).
D. S.

"A" Division.

CRIME REGISTER No :- Mis.No.740/37.

Diary Number:- 2. Nature of Offence:-

Time at which investigation begun and concluded each day
Places visited in course of investigation each day

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Mr.M.C.Ford, Manager of The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, 14.I.C., Route Edouard VII, who could not be interviewed on the evening of October 12th 1937, was seen by the undersigned about 9.30 a.m.on October 13th 1937 at his office at the mentioned address with reference to the publication of former date, which alleged that the Nisshin Kissen Kaisha Building,No. 5, The Bund had been utilised by the Japanese military during the past few days as an observation post to view Pootung. From the facts ascertained by D.S.Hide it was pointed out to him that it was apparent he had possibly submitted the story of hearsay. He stated a certain foreigner in an office nearby had informed him about having seen Japanese military and latterly a Japanese in plain clothes keeping observation from the location stated. However, on the morning of October 12th 1937 two of their photographers kept watch on the Nisshin Kissen Kaisha roof with the intent to take photographs of the persons keeping observations from it, but were unsuccessful. Mr.M.C.Ford would not divulge the foreigner's name who informed his office by telephone, consequently it was asked of him to retract the allegation made on the fact he could not substantiate it. Over and above he was strongly

刑事侦缉处（C.I.D.）和签署人进行了查询，并对该大楼从上到下进行了搜查，但未发现任何可疑人员的踪迹。该大楼高十八层，尚未完工。有六名刑事侦缉处警探，编号分别为 464、163、200、213、681 和 □□，夜间在大楼内值班，专门看守大米。除此之外，还有几名由各承包商等雇佣的便衣看守，他们在楼内工作。此外，还有一百多名苦力及其家属居住在那里，由于尚未安装照明系统，大多数人都有电筒。

在询问其中一些苦力时，一名叫 Tsung Yih San（陳一山），48岁，江苏籍，男性/苦力，主动提供信息称，在警探来访前约一刻钟，他观察到一名苦力阶层的中国男子手持电筒下楼。Tsung 睡在二楼，但他曾上到十楼观看炮战。正是在

on this floor that he saw this man, and guessed the time
to be about 12.30 a.m.
Enquiries among the C.P.C.s and watchmen elicited
the fact that there is no check whatsoever on who enters,
there being so many coolies working for different firms,
the majority of which sleep on the premises, that the
watchmen naturally do not know all of them.
As regard the coolie Tsung's story, this would not
seem unusual because as already stated most of the coolies
have flashlights and probably quite a few of them ventured
up to the top floors to view the artillery battle which
was in progress at the time.
It is therefore thought that Major Burke saw the
flashing of lights caused by coolies mounting and
descending the stairs and quite excusably imagined it to
be signalling.

这一层他看到了这个人，并猜测时间大约是凌晨12时30分。
对中国巡捕和看守的询问揭示了一个事实，即对谁进入大楼没有任何检查，因为有这么多苦力为不同的公司工作，其中大多数人住在处所内，看守自然不认识所有人。
至于苦力 Tsung 的说法，这似乎并不奇怪，因为如前所述，大多数苦力都有手电筒，可能有相当一部分人冒险登上顶层观看当时正在进行的炮战。
因此，认为 Burke 少校看到的是苦力上下楼梯时手电筒发出的闪光，并完全可以理解地将其想象为信号。

Subject Shanghai Gas Company alleged to be used as observation post by
Japanese.
Made by C. D. I. Sharman Forwarded by

Sir,
With reference to above allegation made by Col. Sung,
secretary to Gen. Yang Hu, on the afternoon of 4-10-37 I
interviewed Mr. W.J. Baker, Engineer in Chief and Mr. C.F.
Ting, supt of workshops. They both agree that the alle-
gation is without foundation. The only Japanese employee
of the firm (a canvasser) has not been seen since the begin-
ning of hostilities. There is no tower in the ordinary
sense of the word on the premises. There is a small gas
holder at the corner of Yu Ya Ching and Soochow roads about
70 feet high, the roof of which is very difficult of access
and is only visited when repairs have to be carried out.
The workshop is a three-story building about 50 feet high,
and has a flat roof which is easily accessable by stairs.
This roof is sometimes visited by employees but very little
of the Chapei area can be seen from there. A Russian watch-
man is on duty at the gate, day and night, and only employees
with badges and business are allowed on the premises, and as
the workshops are open day and night it is extremely unlikely
that any unauthorised person could be on the premises without
it being generally known.

(Tell Col. Sung his info is timely among others.)

which he much appreciates.

Ting 先生。他们都同意该指控毫无根据。该公司唯一的日本雇员（一名推销员）自战事开始以来就未曾露面。该处所没有通常意义上的塔楼。在虞洽卿路和苏州路拐角处有一个小型储气罐，高约70英尺，其屋顶很难进入，只有在需要进行维修时才会前往。车间是一栋三层建筑，高约50英尺，有一个平坦的屋顶，可以通过楼梯轻松进入。员工有时会去这个屋顶，但从那里几乎看不到闸北地区。门口日夜有一名俄罗斯看守值班，只有佩戴徽章并有公务的员工才被允许进入处所，由于车间日夜开放，任何未经授权的人在不被普遍知晓的情况下进入处所是极不可能的。

特务科主管。

适时获知。 JAW 10月7日

Subject (in full) Newspaper Reports alleging Sinza Road Water Tower being
used by Japanese observers.

Made W. and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross.

In connection with the attached newspaper reports,
a spokesman of the U.S.M.C. Intelligence Office denied that
there was any truth in the report being circulated that
Japanese had been given permission to use or were using the
Shanghai Water Works Company's tower on Sinza Road as an
observation post. He stated, however, that on or about
Sunday, one foreigner and one Japanese in uniform, members
of the S.V.C., attempted to go up the tower but were refused
permission by the American Marines on guard there. He further
stated that since the outbreak of hostilities numerous persons
have sought permission or tried to go up the tower for
observation purposes but all were turned away.

Translation from Russian newspaper "NOVOSTI DNIA" ( Russian
Daily News), September 29,1937. Published by the Russian
Publishing Co. 620 Avenue Foch. Editor- Mr.V.A. Chilikin

JAPANESE VOLUNTEERS WERE SIGNALLING
from S.W.W. Tower.

- Yesterday members of the Japanese Company,S.V.C.,armed
with binoculars and telescopes got on top of the S.W.W.Company's
tower,Sinza Road, and from there signalled to the Japanese,- sta-
ted Mr. C.K.Yui,Mayor of Greater Shanghai,during the course of the
press conference yesterday evening.

- As soon as I received this information from the Chi-
nese Army Headquarters in Shanghai Area -stated the Mayor to repre-
sentatives of the press,- I immediately telephoned to Major K.M.
Bourne,Commissioner of Police of the International Settlement, and
brought this information to his notice. Major Bourne replied that,
indeed, such fact had taken place when two members of the Japanese
Company,S.V.C., got on that tower allegedly out of curiosity,but
were removed from there by the American Marines guarding the sector
where the tower in question is located.

- How could the Japanese volunteers pass through the cor-
don of the American Marines? asked one of the American journalists
Mr. Yui.

- Apparently, by taking advantage of the priviliges they
had as members of a unit which is a part of the Foreign Defence
Force in Shanghai, replied the Mayor.

According to reports of the Chinese Army Headquarters,
continued Mr.O.K.Yui,Japanese observers have been visiting this
tower regularly since September 25 for the purpose of signalling.
The Chinese Army Headquarters upon receipt of the first report to
this effect arranged for a watch to be kept.and after the presence
of the Japanese on the tower had been confirmed, I was communicated
with.

- Why should your snipers not "remove" them from the tower
without mak-
ing any fuss about it ? asked an American journalist.

- This is a remarkable suggestion, I will pass it to the
Chinese Army Headquarters, laughed the Mayor.

译自俄文报纸《NOVOSTI DNIA》（《每日新闻》），1937年9月29日。由俄国出版公司出版，地址：福煦路620号。编辑：V.A. Chilikin 先生

日本志愿者从上海自来水公司塔楼发出信号。

——大上海市市长余井洋先生在昨晚的新闻发布会上表示，昨天，上海义勇队日本连的成员携带双筒望远镜和望远镜登上了新闸路上海自来水公司塔楼的顶部，并从那里向日本人发出信号。

——余市长向新闻界代表表示，一旦我从上海地区中国军队司令部收到此信息，我立即致电国际租界警务处处长 K.M. Bourne 少校，并将此信息告知他。Bourne 少校回答说，确实发生过这样的事实，即上海义勇队日本连的两名成员出于好奇登上了该塔楼，但被守卫该塔楼所在区域的美国海军陆战队员驱离。

——一位美国记者问余先生，日本志愿者是如何穿过美国海军陆战队的警戒线的？

——市长回答说，显然是利用了其作为上海外侨防卫部队一部分的单位成员所享有的特权。

余 O.K. 先生继续说，根据中国军队司令部的报告，日本观察员自9月25日以来一直定期访问该塔楼以发出信号。中国军队司令部在收到第一份此类报告后安排了监视，并在确认日本人出现在塔楼上后，与我取得了联系。

——一位美国记者问，为什么你们的狙击手不干脆把他们从塔楼上“清除”掉，而不必大惊小怪呢？

——市长笑着说，这是一个了不起的建议，我会把它转达给中国军队司令部。

С ВЫШКИ ВОДОНАПОРНОЙ
БАШНИ.

— Чины японской роты Шанхайскаго Волонтерскаго Корпуса вчера днем забрались на водонапорную башню Шанхайской Водопроводной Компании на Синза род, вооруженные винтовками и подзорными трубами и оттуда сигнализировали японцам,— заявил вчера вечером во время пресс-конференции лорд-мэр. Великаго Шанхая О.К. Юй.

— Как только ко мнѣ поступило об этом донесение от штаба китайской армии в шанхайском районѣ—заявил представителям прессы лорд-мэр, я немедленно позвонил начальнику полицейских сил Международнаго Сеттльмента майору К. М. Барн и сообщил ему об этом. Майор Барн мнѣ отвѣтил, что такой факт действительно имѣлъ мѣсто, когда два чина японской роты Шанх. Волонтерскаго Корпуса забрались на башню, якобы из любопытства, но были удалены оттуда американскими маринами, которые несут охрану сектора, в котором находится водонапорная башня Шанхайской Водопроводной Компании.

— Каким же образом японские волонтеры прошли через кордон американских марин?—задает вопрос один из американских журналистов мэру Юй.

— Повидимому, пользуясь своими привилегіями чинов или сами японцы отвтят отряда, входящаго в состав на этот вопрос?
шанхайскаго иностраннаго — Судя по тѣм ужасам,
охраннаго гарнизона — от- которые переживают мир-
вѣтил мэр. ные жители и разсматривая
— Согласно сообщеній раненія пострадавших, —
китайскаго штаба, японскіе можно судить, что един-
наблюдатели посѣщали эту ственной страной, которая
башню регулярно с 25 в настоящее время произ-
сентября и производили водит эти пули, является
оттуда сигнализацію. Штаб Японія—добавил мэр Юй.
кит. войск, получив первое Переходя к японским обви-
сообщение установил наблю- неніям о пользовании яко-
деніе и, когда было подтвер- бы китайскими артиллери-
ждено наличіе японцев на стами снарядов, начинен-
этой башнѣ — мнѣ было об ных газом, лорд-мэр заявил,
этом сообщено—продолжал что эта выдумка, нужная
мэр О. К. Юй. для того, чтобы потом,
— Почему-бы вашим снай- употребив газ самим, ссы-
перам было просто не латься на китайцев, что тѣ
«снять» их оттуда? — спра- первые начали газовыя ата-
шивает американский жур- ки — закончил лорд-мэр
налист. О. К. Юй.
— Это замѣчательное
предложеніе, я его передам
китайскому штабу—отвѣтил
со смѣхом лорд-мэр.
— Далѣе лорд-мэр кате-
горически опроверг япон-
скія сообщенія о том, что
в помѣщеніи Муниципальна-
го Совѣта Великаго Шанхая
в Кіангванѣ был найден
контракт с представителями
одной иностранной дежавы
на поставку Китаю
45.000.000 обойм разрывных
пуль «дум-дум».
— Интересно, с каких пор
я, лорд-мэр Великаго Шан-
хая, стал агентом по про-
даж и покупкѣ оружія и
военнаго снаряженія? —
смѣясь спросил лорд-мэр.
Может быть кто нибудь

——一位美国记者问，为什么你们的狙击手不干脆把他们从那里“清除”掉？

——市长笑着回答，这是一个极好的建议，我会将其转达给中国司令部。

——此外，市长坚决驳斥了日本方面的报道，称在大上海江湾市政委员会办公室内发现了一份与某外国政府代表签订的合同，旨在向中国供应4500万发“达姆达姆”扩张型子弹。

——市长笑着问道，有趣的是，我从什么时候起，作为大上海市长，成了武器和军事装备的买卖代理人？也许有人……

page_data.en:
Translation of extract from Russian newspaper SLOVO, September 29,
1937. Published and Editor - Mr. I.M. Altadukeff, 238 Avenue du
Roi Albert.

In conclusion the Mayor stated: " I have received
reports to the effect that beginning from September 26 the fire
of the Japanese artillery in Hongkew has been corrected from the
top of the Shanghai Water Works Tower situated in Sinza Road.
Yesterday, Commander of the Chapei-Markham Road Sector
reported to me by phone that shells were falling nearer and
nearer and asked me to remove the Japanese artillery men from
the said tower. I immediately telephoned to the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police asking them to make investigations into this matter.
The police investigations ascertained that there were two mem-
bers of the Japanese Company, S.V.C., on the tower in question,
who observed the artillery fire through binoculars and corrected
it by signalling to the Japanese batteries. The Police requested
these volunteers who corrected artillery fire to leave the tow-
er of the Shanghai Water Works, a British concern.
Thus an international incident was created.
The fact that teh abovementioned sector is guarded
by the American Marines is also not without a piquant interest."

译自俄文报纸《SLOVO》摘录，1937年9月29日。出版人兼编辑：I.M. Altadukeff 先生，地址：阿尔伯特王路238号。

最后，市长表示：“我收到的报告称，自9月26日起，虹口日本炮兵的射击校正工作是从位于新闸路的上海自来水公司塔楼顶部进行的。昨天，闸北-马克姆路防区指挥官通过电话向我报告，炮弹落点越来越近，并要求我将日本炮兵人员从上述塔楼撤走。我立即致电上海公共租界工部局警务处，要求他们对此事进行调查。警方调查证实，上海义勇队日本连的两名成员确实在该塔楼上，他们通过双筒望远镜观察炮火，并通过向日本炮台发出信号来校正射击。警方要求这些校正炮火的志愿者离开这家英国企业——上海自来水公司的塔楼。
因此，引发了一起国际事件。
上述防区由美国海军陆战队守卫这一事实也颇具讽刺意味。”

page_data.en:
Китайская сводка.

Вчера мэр Великаго Шанхая О. К. Юй сообщил иностранной прессѣ очередную оффиціальную сводку китайскаго штаба дѣйствующей арміи на фронтѣ под Шанхаем.
1. Послѣ затишья въ теченіе двух дней японскіе войска въ секторѣ Лотьена въ понедѣльник и вчера утром показывали значительную активность. Вчера они повели атаку въ большом масштабѣ, но атакующіе были отбиты. Замѣтно, что японскія пушки увеличили дальность своего обстрѣла так, чтобы обстрѣливать поселок Ссу-сіанг-кунг-мяо въ 200 метров къ западу от Лотьена на шоссе Лотьеи-Кадинг.
2. К востоку от Люхонга китайскія войска продолжали удерживать свои позиціи, имѣя центром мост Юнган род. Японскія попытки пробиться через лѣвый фланг китайцев и перерѣзать их линію сообщеній между Дацаном и Люхонгом снова потерпѣли неудачу.
3. По сообщеніям китайских развѣдчиков, проникших въ район Гражданскаго Центра, японскія войска там сооружают прочные окопы вдоль границы этой зоны.
4. Японскіе аэропланы продолжали совершать развѣдку над Чапеем и Путунгом. Вчера утром и днем японскіе бомбовозы снова сбросили там ряд бомб, не причинивших особаго вреда.
5. Вчера на пресс конференціи японцы сообщили, что японскими войсками, занявшими Гражданскій Центр, был обнаружен контракт на покупку 45.000.000 патронов съ пулями «дум дум» у одной иностранной державы. На это мэр задал вопрос «съ каких пор он является агентом по поставкѣ оружія». Японцы не указала страны, въ которой был принят заказ, но, судя по жестокости японцев, проявленной ими против невоюющих граждан, можно предположить, что такой страной фабрикующей 45.000.000 пуль «дум дум» могла быть только Японія.
6. Вчера японскій докладчик снова сообщил о том, что китайцы примѣняют удушливый газ, въ снарядах посылаемых въ японцев. Это сообщеніе абсолютная утка и, видимо, ее японцы распространяют, готовясь къ газовым атакам.
Вчера 12 японских аэроплановъ совершили воздушную бомбардировку Чапея и китайских позицій у Марккам род и Съвернаго вокзала ШНжд. Ущерб причиненный бомбами китайским позиціям очень невеликъ. Отряд японских матросов вчера повел наступленіе на китайскіе позиціи въ Чапеѣ от Джу-конг род, но это наступленіе было отбито китайцами, потерявшими одного убитаго и 3 раненых. У японцев потери от 8-10 матросов. Общее положеніе въ Чапеѣ прочное и, как заявил О. К. Юй по телефону, командир этого участка доложил мэру, что он считает позиціи въ Чапеѣ неприступными. До сих пор всѣ атаки японцев въ Чапеѣ разбивались о солидныя укрѣпленія и мужество китайских солдат.
На запрос журналистов о потерях японцев въ Шанха, мэр отвѣтил, что точно он не знает, но думает что не менѣе 10.000 убитых и раненых. Численность японских войск подъ Шанхаем он опредѣляет въ 130 000 штыков. На вопрос журналистов о заявленіи японскаго докладчика, что китайскіе солдаты плохо питаются, мэр отвѣтил, что въ начал военных дѣйствій вопрос был дѣйствительно острым, но съ тѣх пор снабженіе арміи продуктами налажено. Въ заключеніе вчерашней бесѣды мэр сообщил о слѣдующем.//«Я получил донесеніе, что съ 26-го сентября стрѣльба японской артиллеріи из Хончжоу корректируется съ водокачки шанхайскаго водопровода, расположенной на Синза род. Вчера командир участка въ Чапеѣ и Марккам род звонил мнѣ по телефону и сообщил, что снаряды ложатся все ближе и ближе и просил убрать японских артиллеристов съ водокачки... Я немедленно позвонил полицейским властям ШМС и просил их разслѣдовать обстоятельство. При провѣркѣ вопроса полиціей выяснилось, что на водокачкѣ находились два японских волонтера ШНК, которые наблюдают въ бинокль за стрѣльбой, корректировали ее, сигнализируя японским батареям для болѣе точной стрѣльбы... Этих волонтеров японской роты, корректировавших стрѣльбу съ водокачки англійской «Уотер Уоркс» полиція попросила удалиться. Таким образом создался международный инцидент. Пикантным обстоятельством является также то, что названный сектор охраняется американскими матросами.
page_data.zh:
中文摘要。

昨日，大上海市长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）向外国新闻界发布了中国军队上海前线司令部最新的官方战报。
1. 经过两天的沉寂后，日军在罗店（Lotien）防区于周一及昨晨表现出显著的活动。昨日他们发动了大规模进攻，但进攻者被击退。值得注意的是，日军火炮增加了射程，以便轰击位于罗店以西200米、罗店-嘉定（Kaading）公路上的四象公庙（Ssu-siang-kung-miao）村落。
2. 在刘行（Liuhong）以东，中国军队继续坚守阵地，以永安桥（Yungan bridge）为中心。日军试图突破中国军队左翼并切断其在大场（Dachan）与刘行之间的交通线的企图再次失败。
3. 据潜入市中心（Civilian Center）区域的中国侦察员报告，日军正在该区域边界沿线构筑坚固的战壕。
4. 日本飞机继续在闸北（Chapei）和浦东（Putung）上空进行侦察。昨日上午和下午，日本轰炸机再次在该地区投下多枚炸弹，未造成特别严重的损害。
5. 昨日在记者招待会上，日方称，占领市中心的日军发现了一份向某外国购买45,000,000发“达姆达姆”（dum dum，即扩张型）子弹的合同。对此，市长反问：“他从何时起成了武器供应代理人？”日方未指出接受订单的国家，但鉴于日军对非战斗人员表现出的残暴，可以推测，制造这45,000,000发“达姆达姆”子弹的国家只能是日本。
6. 昨日，日本发言人再次声称，中国在射向日军的炮弹中使用窒息性毒气。这一消息纯属捏造，显然是日方在为发动毒气攻击做准备而散布的谣言。
昨日，12架日本飞机对闸北以及马克汉姆路（Markham road）和上海北站（North Railway Station of SH.R.）附近的中国阵地进行了空中轰炸。炸弹对中国阵地造成的损害非常轻微。昨日，一队日本水兵从朱公桥（Chu-kong bridge）方向向闸北的中国阵地发起进攻，但该进攻被中国人击退，中方一死三伤。日方伤亡水兵8至10人。闸北的总体局势稳固，正如俞鸿钧在电话中所言，该地段指挥官向市长报告称，他认为闸北的阵地坚不可摧。迄今为止，日军在闸北的所有进攻都撞在中国士兵坚固的工事和勇气上而粉碎。
当记者询问日军在上海的伤亡情况时，市长回答说他并不确切知道，但认为死伤人数不少于10,000人。他估计上海附近的日军兵力为130,000支步枪。针对记者关于日本发言人声称中国士兵伙食不佳的提问，市长回答说，在战争初期这个问题确实很严峻，但此后军队的粮食供应已得到妥善安排。在昨日谈话的最后，市长通报了以下情况：“我收到报告，自9月26日起，日军从虹口（Hongzhou）进行的炮击是由位于新闸路（Sinza road）的上海自来水公司水塔进行校正的。昨日，闸北和马克汉姆路地段的指挥官通过电话向我报告，说炮弹落点越来越近，并要求将日本炮兵从水塔上撤走……我立即致电工部局警务处当局，请求他们调查此事。经警方核查，发现水塔上有两名日本上海义勇队（S.V.C.）志愿者，他们正用双筒望远镜观察炮击情况，并通过向日本炮台发出信号来校正射击，以提高精度……警方要求这些在英国‘自来水公司’（Water Works）水塔上校正射击的日本连队志愿者离开。从而引发了一起国际事件。另一个微妙的事实是，该区域由美国水兵守卫。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 1937

WATERWORKS' TOWER
NOT SIGNAL POST

Denial Of Reported Use
By Japanese Issued
By Mr. Pearson

Mr. C. D. Pearson, engineer-in-chief and manager of the Shanghai Waterworks Co., Ltd., wrote to Mayor O. K. Yui yesterday calling the latter's 'attention to the statement made by a Chinese military spokesman at the press conference on Monday about the use of a water-tower on Sinza Road by the Japanese for observation and signalli ; purposes.
The statement was described as "incorrect" in Mr. Pearson's letter, which reads in part:
"The company's property in which the water-tower is situated, is occupied by members of the U.S. Marines who on Sunday last prevented certain officers of the S.V.C. from ascending the tower."
It was alleged by a Chinese military spokesman on Tuesday that the water tower had been used by Japanese since Saturday to signal to Japanese aeroplanes bombing Chapei. An immediate denial of the statement was issued by officials of the Shanghai Waterworks, who declared that unauthorized persons were prevented by the Marines guarding the Company's property from access to the tower.

自来水厂水塔
并非信号站

皮尔逊先生发布声明
否认有关日军使用的报道

上海自来水有限公司总工程师兼经理C. D. 皮尔逊（C. D. Pearson）先生昨日致函俞鸿钧市长，提请后者注意一位中国军方发言人在周一记者招待会上所作的关于日军利用新闸路（Sinza Road）上一座水塔进行观察和信号联络的声明。
皮尔逊先生在信中称该声明“不实”，信件部分内容如下：
“该水塔所在的公司产业由美国海军陆战队队员驻守，他们在上周日阻止了上海义勇队（S.V.C.）的某些官员登上水塔。”
周二，一位中国军方发言人声称，自周六以来，该水塔一直被日军用于向轰炸闸北的日本飞机发送信号。上海自来水公司官员立即发表声明否认了这一说法，宣称 guarding 公司产业的美国海军陆战队阻止了未经授权的人员进入水塔。

Marines, Waterworks Co. Deny
Tower Occupied By Observers

United States Marine Corps authorities denied yesterday that the Sinza Road water tower, located in their defense sector, was ever used by Japanese for observation purposes.

It was explained that when two Japanese S. V. C. members attempted to enter the tower Sunday, they were refused permission to and asked to leave the premises.

Pearson Denies Statement

Mr. C. D. Pearson, engineer-in-chief and manager of the Shanghai Waterworks Co., Ltd., wrote to Mayor O. K. Yui today calling the latter's attention to the statement made by a Chinese military spokesman at the press conference on Monday about the use of a water-tower on Sinza Road by the Japanese for observation and signalling purposes, says Central News.

The statement was described as "incorrect" in Mr. Pearson's letter, which reads in part:

"The company's property in which the water-tower is situated, is occupied by members of the U. S. Marines who on Sunday last prevented certain officers of the S.V.C. from ascending the tower."

CHINA PRESS - 29.9.37.
25837

Japanese Using Water Tower
In American Defense Sector
As Observation Post Ejected

Japanese observers, using highpower binoculars, had been sta-
tioned on top the Sinza Road water tower of the Shanghai Water
Works during the past few days to watch Chinese troop positions
and to direct Nipponese aerial and artillery bombardments in Cha-
pei, the Chinese military spokesman disclosed to newsmen at the
press conference yesterday afternoon.
Persistent reports, the spokesman said, had been received by the
Chinese military authorities that the tower was being used by the
Japanese as a look-out post. Upon investigations, the spokesman
was informed yesterday that two Japanese S.V.C. members had been
seen entering the tower. The two Japanese, the spokesman stated,
were subsequently ejected from the tower by the foreign defense
troops in the Sinza Road area.
Authorities of the United States Marine Corps, in whose sector
the tower is located, informed THE CHINA PRESS last night that on
Sunday two Japanese were ejected from the tower. Since that day,
it was stated, a sentry has been posted in the tower and no one is
being allowed to enter the structure.

《大美晚报》 - 1937年9月29日
25837

作为观察哨使用水塔的日本人
在美軍防御区内被驱逐

中国军方发言人在昨日下午的记者招待会上向记者透露，过去几天里，日本观察员一直驻扎在上海自来水公司新闸路（Sinza Road）水塔的顶部，使用高倍双筒望远镜监视中国军队阵地，并引导日军在闸北（Chapei）进行空中和炮兵轰炸。
该发言人称，中国军方当局收到了关于该水塔被日军用作瞭望哨的持续报告。经调查，发言人昨日获悉，有人看到两名日本上海义勇队（S.V.C.）成员进入水塔。该发言人 stated，这两名日本人随后被新闸路地区的外国防御部队逐出水塔。
水塔所在区域的美国海军陆战队当局昨晚告诉《大美晚报》，周日有两名日本人被逐出水塔。据称，自那以后，水塔内已部署了一名哨兵，不允许任何人进入该建筑。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1937

A Misapprehension
Inquiry of the Shanghai Water-
works Company elicits the infor-
mation that the Chinese military
spokesman is under a misappre-
hension. The Company has taken
and is continuing to take full pre-
cautions to see that its premises
are not used for observation pur-
poses by unauthorised persons. The
tower in question has been under
the guard of the American
Marines who have seen to it that
no access to it is given to in-
truders. That vigilance, indeed,
gave rise to the incident to which
the Chinese spokesman referred
but of which he evidently had
imperfect information. What
happened was that on Sunday a
non-British, non-American officer
of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps
with two Japanese friends pre-
sented themselves at the tower
with the apparent intention of
ascending it to view the sur-
rounding country. They were at
once challenged by the American
Marines on guard and an officer of
the Marine ordered them to leave
the premises at once which they
did. The ill-advised visit therefore
had no success.

《字林西报》，1937年9月29日，星期三

一种误解

对上海自来水公司的查询获悉，中国军方发言人存在误解。该公司已经并正在采取充分预防措施，确保其场所不被未经授权的人员用于观察目的。涉事水塔一直由美国海军陆战队守卫，他们确保入侵者无法进入。事实上，正是这种警惕性引发了中国发言人所提及的事件，但他显然对该事件的信息掌握不全。实际情况是，周日，一名非英籍、非美籍的上海义勇队军官带着两名日本朋友来到水塔，明显意图登塔眺望周边乡村。他们立即受到执勤的美国海军陆战队的质询，一名海军陆战队军官命令他们立即离开该场所，他们照办了。因此，这次欠考虑的访问并未成功。

Made by P.S. 355. Forwarded by Insp. 1/c.

Sir,
At 9.10.p.m. September 14th 1937, a telephone
message was received at Gordon Road Police Station, from the
British Military Headquarters, requesting the services of the
police at the Kung Yih (公益) Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road.
The undersigned accompanied by D.S.I. Chu Meng ei
attended and on arrival at the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, were met
Captain Hickson and Lieutenant Rogers, the former being the
officer in charge of the detachment of British soldiers stat-
ioned on the premises.
Captain Hickson stated that he had been informed by
Mr Davies, manager of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, to the effect
that on several nights when Chinese aeroplanes were heard in
the vicinity tracer bullets or red flares immediately appeared
in the air and came from the direction of the Kung Dah (公大)
Cotton Mill, 59/60 Singapore Road.
Captain Hickson, Lieutenant Rogers, J.P.S. 24 and
the undersigned proceeded to the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, where
Mr E. Ruvalcaba, manager of the concern was interviewed and at
the request of the two above named officers gave permission to
search the premises.
Three large electric bulbs, red, white and green in
colour were found in the observation post situated on the West
side of the premises. The current was disconnected at the switch
board, but could be connected in the case of emergency to a
temporary dynamo in the barbers shop. Nothing further of a
suspicious nature was found on the premises.

D.D.O.
"B" Div.
J Coyne A.S.I

署名人与副巡官朱孟义（Chu Meng ei）一同前往，抵达公益纱厂时，遇到了希克森上尉（Captain Hickson）和罗杰斯中尉（Lieutenant Rogers），前者是驻扎在该处的英军分遣队负责人。

11th Sept. 37.
Subject Alleged Signalling from the Eastern Times premises
roof, 541 Hooper Road.
Made by D. S. Mac Adie. Forwarded by J. McFarlane C.I.
C./c.

Sir,
At 8.05 p.m. 10.9.37., a telephone message was
received from Mr Merritt, Specials Headquarters, Foochow
Road, to the effect that lights, believed to be signals
had been seen from the Eastern Times premises at 541 Hooper
Road. On receipt of the above message, Insp Williamson and
D. S. Mac Adie proceeded to the Specials hqs and interviewed
Mr Merritt. It was ascertained from the latter that the lights
appeared to come from the roof of the tower of the building
in question but had not been seen since he telephoned.
The above officers kept observation on the building
from 8.20 p.m. until 10.00 p.m. but no signal or light flash
was seen. A visit to the roof of the premises was made and
an examination of the same was carried out but no evidence
of signalling could be found. The officers were detained
for a few minutes on the third floor while a door leading
to the upper part of the building was opened. In the centre
of the handle of this door is a bell which rings in the
manager's quarters, and it is necessary to wait for a
servant to come down and open the door from the inside.
The management through Mr Julian, of the paper, was
informed of the complaint. Mr Julian gave assurance that
the roof of the said building would be kept clear of all
persons after dark.
There is a radio station and a dark room in the building
and it is possible that the light came from these, or were
reflections from the panes of a bulkhead door on the tower
roof.

R.W. Mac Adie.
D. S.

1937年9月11日。
事由：据称有人从虎丘路541号《字林西报》馆屋顶发出信号。
呈报人：D. S. Mac Adie（巡长）。经由警探长 J. McFarlane 转呈。
抄送。

先生：
1937年9月10日晚上8点05分，福州路后备警察总部 Merritt 先生打来电话，称有人看见虎丘路541号《字林西报》馆（Eastern Times） premises 处有灯光，疑似为信号。接到上述消息后，Williamson 督察和 D. S. Mac Adie 前往后备警察总部并会见了 Merritt 先生。据后者告知，灯光似乎是从该建筑塔楼的屋顶发出的，但自他打电话以来便未再见到。
上述警官从晚上8点20分至10点00分对该建筑进行了监视，但未发现任何信号或闪光。随后对场所屋顶进行了视察和检查，但未发现任何发信号的证据。在打开通往建筑上层的门时，警官们在三楼停留了几分钟。该门把手中央有一个铃，会在经理宿舍响起，因此需要等待仆人下来从内部开门。
通过该报社的 Julian 先生，管理层已获悉此投诉。Julian 先生保证，天黑后将确保所述建筑的屋顶上没有任何人员。
该建筑内有一个无线电台和一个暗室，灯光可能来自这些地方，或者是塔楼屋顶舱口门玻璃上的反光。

R.W. Mac Adie.
D. S.

At 6.30 p.m. 3/9/37 a report was received from
Mr. Uyehara D.C.Japanese, to the effect that he had
received information from the Japanese Consulate that
flash-light signals were being made from the top of
the Capitol Theatre before Chinese artillery went into
action at Pootung on the morning of the 3/9/37.

The undersigned, D.S.Francis and C.D.S.205 visited
the above building and interviewed the caretaker of the
premises, named Mr.J.E.Parkoff Russian, After examining
the roof nothing could be found which would substantiate
the allegation re making a signal.

Mr. J.E. Parkoff was subsequently warned not to
allow any Chinese or unknown persons to proceed to the
roof for sight seeing in order to prevent any unexpected
incident.

A further visit will be made after day-break on the
4-9-37 as it is surmised that the sun was reflecting on
a neon sign-board which situated on the top of the
building.

Date September 5, 19 37.

Subject Signals emanating from a spot near the Bus Company Depot,
        Connaught Road.

Made by D.S. Pitts            Forwarded by [Signature]

A visit was paid to the China General Omnibus Company
Ltd., 1117 Connaught Road, during the afternoon of September 4,
1937, when it was learned from Mr. D.J. Chandler, Traffic
Manager, that during day light hours of the past week white
lights, apparently signals to passing Japanese planes, have
been observed emanating from a spot some 300 yards south-west
of the Bus Company's premises. This spot is in Chinese
territory.

Mr. Chandler also stated that since hostilities commenced,
an occasional rifle shot has been heard, apparently from a spot
some 150 yards due west of the Company's premises. This only
occurs when Japanese planes are overhead. This spot is also
in Chinese territory.

Apart from the above details no further information could
be obtained from the foreign staff of the Company.

D.S. Pitts.

1937年9月4日下午，走访了位于康纳路1117号的中国通用巴士有限公司，从交通经理 D.J. Chandler 先生处获悉，在过去一周的白天时段，有人观察到白光从巴士公司场所以西南约300码处发出，这些光显然是向过往的日本飞机发出的信号。该地点位于中国领土内。

REPORT

Subject Rumours of signalling lights in Lootoo and Gordon Road Districts.

Made by D.S.Hocking Forwarded by C. Crawford D.O

The Kung Dah No.3 Mill, 58 and 60 Singapore Road, is
at present housing some eighty Japanese civilians, all
employees of the Kung Dah mills. Several shot-guns and
sporting rifles, the personal property of certain employees
of the Kung Dah mills, have always been kept on the premises
and are there at present, as far as can be ascertained. On the
roof of the mill is the usual signal tower typical of Japanese
mills and factories in Shanghai but no sign of signal lights
is to be observed.

It was reported that a red beam was seen rising into the
sky from the area around Robison Road and Tonguin Roads during
the early morning of August 30. As far as is known no further
beams of any description have been observed in that vicinity.

The Kiwa Cotton Mill, Japanese concern located at 74
Robison Road, reported as having an anti-aircraft gun on the
roof, has been visited and it can be definitely stated that
no such gun is at present on the roof nor has one been fired
from there during the past two weeks.

D.S.Hocking.

报告

事由：关于卢沟桥路和戈登路地区出现信号灯的谣言。

呈报人：巡长 Hocking 转呈人 C. Crawford 总监

新加坡路58号和60号的公大第三纱厂目前收容了约八十名日本平民，均为公大纱厂的雇员。据查，几支猎枪和运动步枪（属公大纱厂某些雇员的个人财产）一直存放在该场所内，目前仍在那里。纱厂屋顶上有上海日本纱厂和工厂典型的信号塔，但未观察到信号灯迹象。

据报道，8月30日凌晨，有人看到罗宾森路和通金路（音译）附近区域有一束红光射向天空。据所知，此后在该 vicinity 未再观察到任何其他类型的光束。

位于罗宾森路74号的日资企业吉华棉纺厂（音译）据报屋顶装有高射炮，经走访后可明确声明，目前屋顶上没有此类火炮，且在過去两周内也未从那里发射过炮弹。

巡长 Hocking.

Subject Signals alleged to be made in the building of the Toyo Menkwa
Kaisha, 103 Hankow Road.
Made by D.S. Hamashita Forwarded by C. Gaulton S I

With reference to the alleged signalling which took place
on the night of August 25 in the building of the Toyo Menkwa
Kaisha, a Japanese concern at No.103 Hankow Road and is
reported to have been seen by a foreigner in the Hamilton House,
D.S. Hamashita interviewed Mr. Tohmon, manager of the firm
at 4 p.m. August 26 and made an inspection of all parts of the
building.

The building in question is four storied and surrounded by
higher buildings. Parts of the second and third floors can
be seen from the Hamilton House through a space between the
other buildings. One room on the third floor (top) which
can be seen from the Hamilton House is occupied by nine
Chinese, a chauffeur, servants and their families. These
people, when questioned by D.S. Hamashita, denied having used
the lights as signals. An examination of their property
revealed nothing which could be used for signalling, and
there is only one electric lamp in the premises occupied
by them and it is well shaded with paper. Mr. Tohmon stated
that these Chinese are all trusted persons and it is ridiculous
to think that they would do such a stupid act. The other
rooms on the third floor are unoccupied.

Rooms on the second floor which can be seen from the
Hamilton House are occupied by Japanese refugees from the
Dong Shing Cotton Mill and other Japanese firms. The lamps
of these rooms are all well covered with paper. It is
possible that with the window open and the wind blowing that
the suspended electric lights would sway about and convey
the impression that the lamps were being manipulated for a
purpose but it is a mistake. The Japanese refugees living

关于8月25日晚在汉口路103号日资企业东洋棉花株式会社大楼内发生的据称发信号事件，据报道一名住在汉密尔顿大厦的外国人看见了该情况，巡长 Hamashita 于8月26日下午4点会见了该公司经理 Tohmon 先生，并对大楼的所有部分进行了检查。

该建筑为四层楼，周围被更高的建筑环绕。透过其他建筑之间的空隙，可以从汉密尔顿大厦看到二楼和三楼的部分区域。三楼（顶层）的一个房间可从汉密尔顿大厦看到，里面住着九名中国人，包括一名司机、仆役及其家属。这些人接受巡长 Hamashita 询问时，否认使用灯光作为信号。对其财产的检查未发现任何可用于发信号的物品，且他们居住的场所内只有一盏电灯，并用纸很好地遮蔽了光线。Tohmon 先生表示，这些中国人都是可信之人，认为他们会做出如此愚蠢的行为是荒谬的。三楼的其他房间无人居住。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.......... 8395
REPORT
Date August 27, 1937.

Subject Conservation duty carried out in vicinity of 116 Jessfield
Road - Japanese premises occupied by Mr. Yamamoto.

Made by: .................... Forwarded by: A. S. Lockwood.

From August 16 - August 25, 1937, observation duty
by the undersigned and Chinese detectives was carried out
in the vicinity of 116 Jessfield Road, premises occupied by
a Japanese named Mr. Yamamoto, manager of the Kung Shing Co. 1
Cotton Mill, as it was reported that signalling had been
observed from the top windows.

Although a number of 'Verey lights' have been seen,
which reportedly were fired in Chinese territory, no
signalling by means of 'flash' or 'coloured lights' had
been observed. One incident occurred, however, during the
evening of August 24, 1937, when at 10 p.m. a Japanese constable
(number unknown) entered the premises. He remained in the
house for approximately one hour and then departed in the
direction of Bubbling Well Road.

Mr. J.W. Gray, an employee of the Bank of China,
residing at 400 Avenue Haig, informed the police as to the
alleged activities in the house. When interviewed he stated
that he had received this information from some of his
colleagues in the Bank of China who, in turn, had received
it from some other source. In order to alleviate the
feelings of his associates, he had passed this information
to the police authorities for what it was worth.

报告
日期：1937年8月27日。

事由：在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）116号附近执行的守卫任务——山本先生占据的日方产业。

制作人：.................... 转呈人：A. S. Lockwood。

1937年8月16日至8月25日期间，由具名者及华籍侦探在极司菲尔路116号附近执行观察任务，该处房产由一名名为山本先生的日本人占据，其身份为公兴纱厂（Kung Shing Co. Cotton Mill）经理，此前有报告称从顶层窗户观察到信号活动。

虽然据报在中国领土方向发射了多枚“维里灯”（Verey lights，即信号弹），但并未观察到通过“闪光”或“彩色灯光”进行的信号传递。然而，在1937年8月24日晚间发生了一起事件，当晚10时，一名日本巡捕（编号不详）进入该处房产。他在屋内停留约一小时后，朝静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）方向离去。

中国银行职员J.W. Gray先生，居住在海格路（Avenue Haig）400号，向警方通报了该房屋内的涉嫌活动。在接受问询时，他表示该信息得自其在中国银行的一些同事，而这些同事又是从其他来源获知。为了消除其同事的疑虑，他将此信息转告警方当局，供参考斟酌。

File No. 8039A
Section 1, Special Branch Station, 37
REPORT
Date August 26, 1937

Subject Signals flashed from 103 Hankow Road.

Made by D.S. Locking Forwarded by C. Coulson. DJ

The above address is a four story building on the south
side of Hankow Road east of Szechuen Road in which are located
eight Japanese firms. The roof of the building is of sheet
metal sloping on four sides and not accessible from below.
Let into the roof are two glass skylights through which the
signalling on the night of August 24 appeared to come. Owing
to the height of the surrounding buildings it is impossible
to send signals laterally and as at the time signalling was
being carried on, air-craft were flying, it might be assumed
that the recipient of these signals was in the air. Since
the night of August 24 no further signals have been observed
but a watch on the building will be continued.

D.S. Locking

Subject Report by Light Horse Company, S.V.C., of Light Flashes from
15th Floor, Park Hotel, seen at 9.45 p.m. August 24, 1937.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

K. I. V.
MB
26 AUG 1937

On the morning of August 25, 1937, Major E.H. McMichael,
S.V.C., reported to Major A.S.G. Douglas, Brigade Major, S.V.C.,
that members of the Light Horse Company, S.V.C., billeted in the
Race Course, had seen flashes of light which appeared to be
signalling, coming from what was believed to be the 15th Floor
of the Park Hotel, at 9.45 p.m. August 24, 1937.

D. C. in C.
In consequence of this information, members of the
Special Branch interviewed Mr. Schibler, Manager of the Park
Hotel, at 11 a.m. August 25, and ascertained that a flat on the
15th Floor is used by Mr. Z.L. Loo, Director of the Park Hotel,
but that since the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities, Mr. Loo
has not made use of the place. Also that from the 14th Floor
(Ballroom) upwards, the remaining floors are vacant and
inaccessible to anyone except the staff. Enquiries among the
various members of the latter elicited a denial that any
signalling had been done from the Park Hotel. An examination
of the various floors from the 14th Floor upwards failed to reveal
any signs of signalling apparatus, but this fact does not dispose
of the allegation that light flashes were seen.

Mr. Schibler stated that in order to ensure that no
unauthorised person can make use of the Park Hotel tower, he
will have that part of the building from, and including the 14th
Floor upwards, locked and the only persons admitted will be the
elevator mechanics whose duty requires that they remain on top
of the tower where the elevator motors are located.

鉴于此信息，特别分部成员于8月25日上午11时会见了国际饭店经理Schibler先生，并查明15层的一套公寓由国际饭店董事Loo Z.L.先生使用，但自中日敌对行动爆发以来，Loo先生一直未使用该处。此外，从14层（舞厅）往上，其余楼层均空置，除工作人员外任何人不得进入。在对后者各类成员的询问中，均否认有人从国际饭店发出信号。对14层及以上各楼层的检查未发现任何信号装置痕迹，但这一事实并不能驳斥看到闪光的说法。

Schibler先生表示，为确保无人未经授权利用国际饭店塔楼，他将把包括14层在内的以上部分建筑上锁，唯一允许进入的人员是电梯技工，因其职责要求他们必须停留在安装电梯马达的塔楼顶部。

February 2, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Iao (February 1) and other local newspapers :-

WOOSUNG-SHANGHAI SPECIAL CHINESE CORPS LEAVE SHANGHAI

According to information secured from reliable sources, the last batch of armed Chinese units who were active in Shanghai, including the International Settlement and the French Concession, have now announced their departure from this locality. These armed Chinese units have always been treated as a terrorist body. They are under the control of the Military Affairs Commission of the Chinese Government. Not only were the Japanese military authorities much annoyed by the activities of these Chinese units, but the authorities of the Foreign Settlements experienced considerable trouble because of their activities.

These armed Chinese units are named the "Woosung-Shanghai Special Chinese Corps" and had been stationed in this locality since the evacuation of the Chinese armies. Under the leadership of Captain Hsiung (熊), these Special Chinese Corps have now secretly withdrawn from Shanghai.

The Corps issued a farewell letter upon its departure from Shanghai, in which it states :- "Without knowledge of the true facts, the authorities of the Foreign Settlements regarded the Special Chinese Corps as a terrorist body and began to arrest people recklessly with the result that many innocent persons have been arrested. For the safety of the residents of the Foreign Settlements and for the convenience of our work and according to instructions received, we are now withdrawing from the areas of the Foreign Settlements".

It seems that the Japanese intelligence authorities had previous knowledge of the transfer of the Special Chinese Corps. Last week, the Japanese Shanghai Newspaper Censorship Bureau notified Chinese papers that the publication of news relating to the Corps is prohibited.

The death of most of the Chinese traitors may have been the work of the Corps.

Standard and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE MOBILE UNITS REOCCUPY CHWANSHA AND NANHWEI

Some time ago fighting took place between Japanese troops and the Chinese mobile units at Fengsien, Nanhwei and Chwansha. According to a person from Chwansha, the fighting was not so serious as reported. The Japanese troops have voluntarily withdrawn from the walled cities of Chwansha and Nanhwei and these places are again under the occupation of the Chinese units.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition :-

ACTIVITIES OF CHINESE MOBILE UNITS IN HANGCHOW : JAPANESE ARMY COMMANDER KILLED

(金華), According to a telegram received from Kyung Hwa, Chinese mobile units are very active in Hangchow. The other day a member of the unit hurled a hand grenade at a Japanese army commander named Yanagimura and three gendarmes. The commander was killed.

1938年2月2日。上午译文。

《大美晚报》（2月1日）及其他本地报纸：-

吴淞-上海特别中国部队离开上海

据从可靠渠道获得的消息，最后一批在上海（包括公共租界和法租界）活动的武装中国部队现已宣布撤离该地区。这些武装中国部队一直被视为恐怖组织。他们受中国政府军事委员会控制。日本军方当局不仅对这些中国部队的活动感到十分恼火，而且外国租界当局也因其活动而遭受了相当大的麻烦。

这支武装中国部队名为“吴淞-上海特别中国部队”，自中国军队撤离后一直驻扎在该地区。在熊队长（Captain Hsiung）的领导下，这支特别中国部队现已秘密撤出上海。

该部队在离开上海时发布了一封告别信，信中称：“外国租界当局在不了解真实情况的前提下，将特别中国部队视为恐怖组织，并开始随意逮捕人员，导致许多无辜者被捕。为了外国租界居民的安全，以及为了我们工作的便利，并根据收到的指示，我们现在正从外国租界地区撤离”。

看来日本情报当局事先就知道了特别中国部队的转移。上周，日本上海新闻检查局通知中文报纸，禁止刊登与该部队有关的新闻。

大多数汉奸之死可能是该部队所为。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：-

中国游击队重新占领川沙和南汇

不久前，日军与中国游击队在奉贤、南汇和川沙发生了战斗。据一位来自川沙的人士称，战斗并不像报道的那样严重。日军已自愿撤出川沙和南汇的城墙城市，这些地方再次被中国部队占领。

《华美晚报》晨版：-

中国游击队在杭州的活动：日军指挥官被杀

(金华)，据从京华收到的电报，中国游击队在杭州非常活跃。日前，该部队一名成员向一名名叫柳村（Yanagimura）的日军指挥官和三名宪兵投掷手榴弹。该指挥官身亡。

Subject Arrest of a member of the Shanghai Special Service
Corps ( ).
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by (签名)

(左侧批注：Grenade used by FPS Smith)

At 8.50 a.m. October 24, 1937, F.P.S. Smith
(Bubbling Well) was on duty at the Brenan Road Railway
Barrier examining pedestrians and vehicles leaving and
entering the Settlement. For the purpose of facilitating
his work, this officer was operating some ten yards
beyond, or outside, the barrier. At the time mentioned above
he had just examined a truck and had given permission
for it to proceed into Chinese territory, when he was
confronted by two plain clothes Chinese armed with Mauser
pistols, which they pointed at Smith in a threatening
manner. He closed with the nearest Chinese and after a
short struggle succeeded in obtaining possession of the
pistol, and with the assistance of details of the Loyal
Regiment on duty at the barrier, effected his arrest.
The other Chinese managed to escape during the melee.

Searched, the arrested man was in possession of
a hand grenade of the Mills bomb type, as well as the loaded
Mauser pistol and ten rounds of ammunition.

Interrogated at Bubbling Well Station by D.S.
Pitts and D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien, the prisoner gave his
name as Dau Ming Tseu (陶明祖), aged 21, a native of
Shaoshing and stated that he was a first-class member of
the Shanghai Special Service Corps, which he joined some
six weeks ago.

In civilian life, the prisoner is a shop assistant
employed by the Lau Z Sung (老正兴) Repairing and Dyeing
Company, 398 East Seward Road. He avers that in February
or March of this year an advertisement appeared in the
Chinese press to the effect that the Chamber of Commerce

Completing this training, he resumed his civilian employ-

As far as the prisoner knows, the Shanghai
Special Service Corps comprises some 8,000 - 10,000 men,
split into five sections of from 500 to 3,000 members.
These sections are divided into sub-sections, which in
turn are again divided into groups; the latter are also
split up into units of 16 men each.
The Chief of the 3rd Section of the Corps,
the prisoner states, is Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan (朱學范),
Chairman of the Shanghai General Labour Union. This
particular section is mainly engaged in matters affecting
labour control.
The 5th Section, to which the prisoner's unit
belongs, is principally composed of shop workers and
business men and their objective is the locating of
traitors. The chief of his unit is one Wong Zung-ming
(王均明), who was sent to Shanghai by the Nanking
Government.

The Corps, according to the prisoner, was
organized at the beginning of September by the Military
Affairs Commission under orders from General Chiang Kai-
shek, its object being to suppress the activities of
traitors and to generally assist the Chinese military
authorities. (Trench digging, maintenance of law and
order, general police work.)
The headquarters of the Corps is located at
No.1 Sung Ka Zah ( ), near Foong Ling Jao ( ),
Nantao, opposite Route Ghisi, the Chief of the organization
now being General Te Yu-noong ( ) alias Te Lih ( )
who is known to be leader of the Blue Shirts Society,
the former leader, General Wang Chin-chu, having resigned.
Dau Ming fseu's duties as a unit member
consisted of examing pedestrian and vehiclar traffic at
the Brenan Road Barrier in order to see that no traitors
or suspects enter Chinese territory.
The prisoner is quartered in an unnumbered house
on Brenan Road opposite the Sun Sing Cotton Mill, about
400 yards beyond the Railway, and according to his own
story, each member of the unit is armed with a Mauser
pistol, ten rounds of ammunition and four hand grenades -
all being supplied by Colonel Dau Ih San, the leader of
the 5th Section. (The three hand grenades NOT in his
possession when arrested, he states, are in his quarters
as above.)

Date 24th.October, 37.
Subject Arrest of Armed Plain-clothes Soldier at Brenan Road Barrier.
Made by P.S. 148 Smith. Forwarded by
At 8.50p.m. 24/10/37 whilst on duty at Brenan Road
Barrier, I was examining a motor truck as it was passing
through the barrier into Chinese territory. On giving the
driver the "right away" I suddenly found myself confronted
by two Chinese in plain clothes who were both armed and
pointed their pistols at me. I made a grab for the pistol
that was nearest to me and pushed it down.
As soon as I grabbed it, he tried to pull it away from
me but I wrenched it out of his hand. With the assistance of
the British troops he was arrested. I then telephoned the
Station and the Chinese was handed over to D.S. Greenfield.
On searching him, I found a hand grenade in his pocket.
P.S. 148.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.
With reference to the attached extract from the Chinese
newspaper translation containing an unofficial statement from
Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan(朱學范), Chairman of the General Labour
Union, repudiating the report of his participation in any
"special affairs" work, discreet enquiries have been made
and have succeeded in confirming that Mr. Chu has severed
connections with the Shanghai Special Service Corps. A member
of this corps, one Yung Wei-fang(震芳), was arrested by
the Municipal Police on Brenan Road, O.O.L., on September 10,
1937. Another named Fu To-mo(傅多馬) was arrested on
September 16, 1937, on Mapai Road.
According to information received, the Military Affairs
Commission of the National Government decided at the beginning
of this month to organize an "Emergency Period Service Group"
(印：CHINESE INTELLIGENCE OFFICE (23 SEP. 1937) SHANGHAI) (非常時期服務團) in order to cope with the increased activities
of traitors and spies in Shanghai. A sum of $500,000 was
put aside to defray the expenses of this Group, and General
Wong Ching-chiu(王敬玖), Commander of the 87th Division, was
appointed as commander, with Mr. Tu Yueh-sung (杜月笙) and
General Tsai Ching-chun(蔡勁軍), Chief of the Shanghai City
Government Police, as deputies.
A chart showing the organization of this Group is
attached.
On receiving their appointments and instructions,
General Wong Ching-chiu and General Tsai Ching-chun found it
inconvenient in their present positions and the work they
entailed, to actively participate, so left the matter of
organizing this new unit in the hands of Mr. Tu Yueh-sung,
Deputy Commander. In carrying out the organizing of this

    Mr. Tu submitted his recommendation, after the appoint-
ment, to the Military Affairs Commission just as a mere

consequently Mr. Tu has been feeling very annoyed at being
thwarted, and Messrs. Loh Ching-dz and Chu Hsueh-fan have

insulted. In an attempt to clear his name, Mr. Chu Hsueh-
fan caused to be inserted in the Chinese newspapers the
attached translation, while Mr. Tu adopted an indifferent
attitude in the administration of the corps.
    Seeing the attitude of those people, General Tsai,
Chief of the Shanghai City Government Police, decided to
undertake the work himself with the assistance of the Chung
Nyi Association(忠义会), which is composed of Whampoa
cadets, and the headquarters of the group was established
in the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, of which
General Tsai is the Chief. Up to the present two of
the four corps have been formed, namely the Special Service
Corps (特务团) and the Defence and Protection Corps(防护团).

    The officer in charge of the Special Service Corps is

    杜先生在任命后向军事委员会提交了推荐名单，但这仅是一种形式，委员会驳回了这两人的任命，因此杜先生因受阻而感到非常恼火，陆京士和朱学范先生被迫辞去职务，并感到受辱。为了澄清名誉，朱学范先生在中文报纸上刊登了所附译文，而杜先生对该队的管理采取了冷漠态度。

Social Evening News of Sept.12:

MR. CHU HSUEH-FAN ENGAGED IN LABOUR RELIEF WORK

In view of the fact that many factories have
suspended operations and several hundreds of thousands of
workers have been thereby affected ever since the outbreak
of the local hostilities, Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范),
Chairman of the General Labour Union, is busily engaged
in the work for the relief of affected workers.
On the morning of September 11, our reporter
called on Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan and enquired whether he were
very active in certain special affairs work as was reported
recently.
Mr. Chu made the following reply:- "I have
already been very busy in the work for the relief of
workers from war affected zones as well as the international
labour publicity. I did not take part in any special
affairs work. Such a report as is current in this
locality is evidently aimed at misleading the public
and will be dismissed by competent observers.

S /
D.B.H.
1079
page_data.zh:
9月12日《社会晚报》：

朱学范先生从事劳工救济工作

鉴于自本地战事爆发以来，许多工厂停工，数十万工人受到影响，工会总主席朱学范先生正忙于从事受影响工人的救济工作。
9月11日上午，本报记者拜访了朱学范先生，询问他是否如近期报道的那样，在某些特种事务工作中非常活跃。
朱先生回答如下：“我一直忙于战区工人的救济工作以及国际劳工宣传工作。我没有参与任何特种事务工作。本地流传的这种报道显然是为了误导公众，有识之士自会不予理会。

S /
D.B.H.
1079

Made by D.S. Dickson. Forwarded by D. I. Hill

Sir,
At 5.45 p.m. on 21-9-37, S.I's Hue and Hsu brought to the station two boy-scouts named Zung Ching Shing No. 1528(陳琴心) Lui Pah Ling 1521(戴伯林) a/o Taiping Bank Tientsin Road and two male Chinese Hou Bung Ling(茅鵬鴻) newspaper-vendor, residing Nantao and Ling Tuh Foo(林德富), 18, Ningpo, 35 Myburgh Road, from Yu Ya Ching Road near Racecourse Road, where the scouts accused last named of recruiting for plain clothes boy-scouts an organisation, which they stated did not exist.
The undersigned and C.D.3. 11: enquired and ascertained as follows:- At about 5.30 p.m. on 21-9-37, Hao Haung Ling observed Ling Tuh Foo at the corner of Yu Ya Ching and Racecourse Rd with a crowd round him and he was requesting them to become boy-scouts. The observer immediately called the two boy-scouts aforementioned suspecting that Ling Tuh Foo, who was dressed in a white cotton short jacket and black pants was an imposter.
S.I's Huh and Hsu also came on the scene and brought all concerned to the station.
Ling Tuh Foo was thoroughly questioned and gave his story, that he had joined a unit in Nantao to be trained for service at the front but only having been recruited one day previously he knew nothing about the name of his unit, or its origin. He only knew one named Li Kwong Hwei, who had given him a chit(copy of translation attached) to comrades Wong & Zung of the unit he had joined.
Special Branch H.Qrs. were informed and D.S's Lorky and Henchman attended and interrogated Ling Tuh Foo and stated they had no charge to lay against him.

先生，
1937年9月21日下午5时45分，巡长 Hue 和 Hsu 将两名童子军 Zung Ching Shing（编号1528，陳琴心）和 Lui Pah Ling（编号1521，戴伯林），两人均供职于天津路太平银行，以及两名华籍男子 Hou Bung Ling（茅鵬鴻），报贩，居住于南市，和 Ling Tuh Foo（林德富），18岁，宁波人，居住于迈尔西爱路35号，从跑马厅路附近的虞洽卿路带至捕房。童子军指控最后提到的这名男子为一个名为“便衣童子军”的组织招募人员，他们指出该组织并不存在。
署名者及刑事侦缉处第3科第11组警员进行了询问，查明情况如下：1937年9月21日下午5时30分左右，Hao Haung Ling 在虞洽卿路与跑马厅路转角处观察到 Ling Tuh Foo，当时有一群人围着他，他正请求这些人加入童子军。观察者立即叫来上述两名童子军，怀疑身穿白色棉短衫和黑裤的 Ling Tuh Foo 是一名冒充者。
巡长 Huh 和 Hsu 也赶到现场，并将所有相关人员带至捕房。
Ling Tuh Foo 受到详细讯问并陈述了他的经历：他加入了南市的一个单位，接受前线服役训练，但由于前一天才刚被招募，他对自己所属单位的名称或由来一无所知。他只认识一个叫 Li Kwong Hwei 的人，此人给了他一张便条（附译文副本），让他交给他所加入单位里的 Wong 和 Zung 两位同志。
已通知特务处总部，D.S's Lorky 和 Henchman 到场并对 Ling Tuh Foo 进行审讯，表示对他没有指控。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ling Teh Foo, 18, S/haw:er, residing 35 Myburgh
Road.
native of Nin;po. taken by me C.D.3. 112.
translated
Oh. Rd. Stn. on the 21- -37. and interpreted by Clerk Tsung.

At about 9 a.m. on 20-9-37, when I was on Kiukiang Road near
Shantung Road, I observed one named Lee Kwong Mi, age about 30,
Shanghai, newspaper-vendor, residing in Nantao, who gave a speech
as follows:-

"You young fellows must love your country and not to assist
Japanese or to be a traitor. As now in Nantao, they are in need
a number of young plain clothes soldiers, if you wish to join in,
you can follow me."

After we heard the above speech, there were forty of us
followed him to Shanghai; Fellow Countrymen's Association on
Liyuen Road, Nantao.

In the association, Lee Kwong Mi again told us that, if we
wish to received military training as soldiers we may get $9.00
a month as wages and if anyone refused, he can go home. I stayed
there for the night.

At about 4 p.m. on 21-9-37, I found 600 people inside the
Association, all about 18 to 36 years of age, young and strong
fellows, some of them were volunteers and some have received
civilian's military training.

Our captain is one named Zauh, age about 30, put on soldier
uniform, who came to the association at about 4 p.m. to-day and
gave a speech about patriotism.

We have two meals a day, supply by the company. I joined in
the company only one day, so I do not know anything further than
the above. I heard from one of our comrades that, after our
training is completed, we will be transferred to the rear
trenches.

The above is my true statement.

Signed.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下是 Ling Teh Foo，18岁，鞋匠，居住于迈尔西爱路35号。
宁波籍。由我 C.D.3. 112 录取。
翻译
成都路捕房 于 1937年9月21日。由职员 Tsung 口译。

1937年9月20日上午9点左右，当我在靠近山东路的九江路上时，我观察到一名叫 Lee Kwong Mi 的人，年龄约30岁，上海人，报贩，居住于南市，他发表了如下演讲：-

“你们年轻人必须爱国，不要协助日本人或做汉奸。现在南市需要一些年轻的便衣士兵，如果你们愿意加入，可以跟我走。”

听完上述演讲后，我们四十人跟随他前往南市丽园路上海同乡会。

在同乡会里，Lee Kwong Mi 再次告诉我们，如果我们愿意接受士兵军事训练，每月可获得9.00美元工资，如果有人拒绝，可以回家。我在那里过夜。

1937年9月21日下午4点左右，我发现同乡会内有600人，年龄都在18至36岁之间，都是年轻力壮的小伙子，其中有些是志愿者，有些接受过平民军事训练。

我们的队长叫 Zauh，年龄约30岁，身穿军装，他今天下午4点左右来到同乡会，发表了关于爱国主义的演讲。

我们每天吃两顿饭，由公司供应。我加入该公司仅一天，所以除了上述情况外我一无所知。我从一位同志那里听说，训练结束后，我们将被调往后方战壕。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT
Date. September 10, 37.
Subject Arrest of a member of the Shanghai Special Service Corps
(上海市別動隊)
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by

At 2.50 p.m. September 10, 1937, a Chinese, Yung Wei
Fang ( 惲芳 ) was arrested by members of the Bubbling
Well Station some fifteen yards west of Brenan Railway
Crossing (just outside the perimeter) on suspicion of being
an armed robber, a passing postman having pointed him out
as such to the police officers. He did not attempt to
escape and a search of his person resulted in the finding
of a loaded Mauser pistol and thirty rounds of ammunition
concealed inside his jacket.

Interrogated at Headquarters, the prisoner stated
that he was a member of the Shanghai Special Service Corps
which was inaugurated on August 16. It was formed under
the following circumstances, he stated :-

At the outbreak of hostilities, he, with many other
young men, was undergoing a course of civic training at
Kiangyin under General Wang Chin Chu ( 王敬玖 ), Commander
of the 87th Division. On August 16, all the cadets were
sent to Lunghwa by order of the general. At Lunghwa Primary
School the Special Service Corps was established and Chu
Hsueh Van ( 朱學範 ) was appointed Chief of the 2nd Section.

The purpose of the Corps is solely to locate traitors.
Headquarters of the Corps are situated at the Tong Yang
( 東亞 ) Athletic School, Loo Pan Road ( 魯班路 ),
Nantao, its leader being General Wang Chin Chu, Commander
of the 87th Division.

According to the prisoner, the Corps comprises
two Sections, each consisting of six sub-sections, which
each contain twenty members who have all undergone civic
training at Kiangyin.

（印：CITY ... 11 SEP. 1937）

S.1, 特务处 .

事由：逮捕上海特别服务队（上海市別動隊）成员
由 D.S. Pitts 撰写 由 转呈

1937年9月10日下午2时50分，一名华人 Yung Wei Fang（惲芳）在静安寺捕房警员的协助下，在布伦南铁路道口以西约十五码处（刚好在警戒线外）被捕，嫌疑是武装抢劫犯，一名路过邮差向警官指认了他。他没有试图逃跑，对其人身搜查结果在其夹克内发现一支装有子弹的毛瑟手枪和三十发弹药。

在总部受审时，囚犯声称他是上海特别服务队的成员，该队于8月16日成立。他陈述其成立背景如下：-

战事爆发时，他与其他许多青年一起在江阴接受第87师师长王敬玖将军的市民训练课程。8月16日，所有学员奉将军命令被送往龙华。在龙华小学成立了特别服务队，朱學範被任命为第二科科长。

该队的目的纯粹是搜寻汉奸。总队部位于南市鲁班路东亞体育学校，其领导人是第87师师长王敬玖将军。

据囚犯称，该队包括两个科，每科由六个股组成，每股包含二十名成员，这些成员均在江阴接受过市民训练。

the remaining five sub-sections functioning in Nantao.
The headquarters of his sub-section are located in Zang
Loh Li ( 長樂里 ), Heng Fong Road ( 恒丰路 ), Chapei,
under the command of one Wang Yah Ming ( 王映明 ), an
officer of the 87th Division. No pay is received by members,
who are armed with Mauser pistols by their headquarters.
Members of his group sleep and eat at their sub-sectional
headquarters on Heng Fong Road. They operate in Chapei
between Heng Fong Road and Poh Sing Kyung searching for
traitors, they having been sent to this area especially to
assist the 88th Division in this respect. Should any
suspects be arrested they are handed over to the nearest
Police Bureau to be dealt with.
General Yang Hu, Martial Law Commissioner is reported
to have admitted having knowledge of this organization.
According to Mr. Loh Ching Sz ( 陸京士 ), Chief Judge of
the Soong Wu Military Court, the prisoner, with nineteen
others, was sent to join the 88th Division some days ago
and has no right to be in the western district.
The prisoner, who is well known for his terrorist
activities in 1932, and who was charged with attempted
murder in that year in the French Concession, had in his
possession at the time of his arrest :-
(1) a map of Shanghai and environs.

ARREST OF ARMED PLAIN-CLOTHES SOLDIER ON BRENNAN ROAD.O.C.I

At 3.05p.m. 10.9.37 F.S.157 Mills and S.I.Chen
brought to Bubbling Well Station a male Chinese named
Yung Wei Fang(蕙芳) aged 22, native of Zangzhou,
whom they had arrested at 2.50p.m. on Brennan Road in
possession of a Mauser autopistol.

At 2.50p.m. 10.9.37 while F.S.Mills and S.I.Chen
were on duty at the military barrier at the Brennan Road
railway crossing, a postman (name not known) came up to
them and said that there was an armed robber on the road-
way a few yards outside the barrier. The postman walked
outside the barrier and indicated the man he referred to
by standing behind him. The two officers mentioned,
arrested Yung Wei Fang who was wearing a black Sun Yat
Sen style jacket and white pants and a blue student type
hat. He was searched and found to possess the following:

(1) One long barrelled Mauser autopistol No.35649
which he was carrying concealed in the inside left
pocket of his jacket. One round of ammunition was
in the breech.

(2) Two magazines and 30 rounds of ammunition(which
includes the round in the breech of the pistol).

(3) One cotton tab(not attached to his jacket but
loose in his pocket) bearing the following -
"Shanghai Special Service Corps Hq. 1st.Sub-
Section of the 2nd. Division. Number Yung Wei Fang.
Badge No.60456."

(4) One map of Shanghai and environs.

(5) One metal pendant issued by the 16th.Branch of
the 1st. District Citizens' Federation.

1.

在布伦南路逮捕武装便衣士兵。O.C.I

1937年9月10日下午3时05分，F.S.157 Mills 和巡长 Chen 将一名名叫 Yung Wei Fang (蕙芳) 的22岁华籍男子带至静安寺捕房，该男子系常州人，他们于下午2时50分在布伦南路将其逮捕，当时他持有一支毛瑟自动手枪。

1937年9月10日下午2时50分，当 F.S. Mills 和巡长 Chen 在布伦南路铁路道口的军事路障处执勤时，一名邮差（姓名不详）走近他们说，路障外几码处的道路上有一名武装抢劫犯。邮差走到路障外，站在那个人身后指认了他。上述两名警官逮捕了 Yung Wei Fang，他身穿黑色中山装式夹克、白色裤子和蓝色学生帽。经搜查，发现他持有以下物品：

(1) 一支长管毛瑟自动手枪，编号35649，藏在其夹克左侧内袋中。枪膛内有一发子弹。

(2) 两个弹匣和30发子弹（包括手枪枪膛内的那一发）。

(3) 一个棉质标签（未缝在夹克上，而是松散地放在口袋里），上面写着 -
“上海特别服务队总部。第二科第一股。编号 Yung Wei Fang。徽章号60456。”

(4) 上海及周边地区地图一份。

(5) 第一特区市民联合会第十六分会颁发的金属吊坠一枚。

page_data.en:
SMP/31 P.Y.
1/sheet 2.

(6) Two name cards. One his own, and the other in the
name of a friend Li Sih Tseng(李錫珍)。

Yung Wei Fang was recognised by detectives as having
been arrested in 1938 for terrorist acts in connection
with the "Blood and Souls" group (血魂除奸團)。
He admitted his identity and stated that he had joined
a citizen's training squad at the end of June 1937 and
on 14.8.37 he joined the Special Service Corps. He
added that the pistol was issued to him each time he went
on duty from the H.Q. of the sub-section to which he is
attached at Zang Loh Lee(長樂里) off Hang Feng Road,
Chapei. He stated that the seized pistol was issued to
him at 6a.m. 10.9.37 and he was instructed to go to the
Brenan-Jessfield Roads area and look for traitors and
spies.

Owing to the past record of Yung Wei Fang, and there
being some connection between the Special Service Corps
and the 57th, & 88th. Divisions of the Chinese Army, the
Special Branch was informed and the prisoner taken there
for further examination. At the request of C.D.I. Ross
Sp.Br. Yang Wei Fang is being held until 11.9.37 for
further enquiry.

The seized pistol, magazines and ammunition were
handed over to Supt.MacDermott P.A./D.C.(Crime).

The fingerprints of Yung Wei Fang were checked and
his record is :-

till 19/9

侦探认出雍伟芳（Yung Wei Fang）曾于1938年因与“血魂除奸團”有关的恐怖活动而被捕。
他承认了自己的身份，并称他于1937年6月底加入了一支市民训练队，并于1937年8月14日加入了特别服务队。他补充说，每次他执勤时，手枪都是由他所隶属的分部总部发放的，该分部位于闸北恒丰路附近的长乐里（Zang Loh Lee）。他说，被缴获的手枪是1937年9月10日上午6点发给他的，他受命前往布伦南路（Brenan Road，今南昌路）和杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road，今中山公园路）地区搜寻汉奸和间谍。

鉴于雍伟芳的过往记录，且特别服务队与中国军队第57师和第88师之间存在某种联系，特科（Special Branch）已获知此事，囚犯已被带往那里接受进一步审查。应特科罗斯（Ross）警司的要求，杨伟芳（Yang Wei Fang，注：此处原文名字拼写与前文略有不同）将被拘留至1937年9月11日，以待进一步调查。

被缴获的手枪、弹夹和弹药已移交给犯罪科副主管麦克德莫特（MacDermott）警司。

4 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Fu Tu-ma (傅多馬)
native of Tinghai taken by me D. S. Larby
at Police Hqrs. on the 16.9.37 and interpreted by D.I. Pan Lien-pih

My name is Fu Tu-ma (傅多馬), age 27, native of Tinghai,
Chekiang, formerly principal of and at present living at the
Sing Kwang Primary School(新光小学), Chang Shing Li Alleyway
(長興里), Chang Shing Road, Chapel.

On August 20, 1937, I joined the Investigation Section of
the Special Service Company Headquarters which is under the
command of one Liu Hwai(刘槐), Chief of the Detective Squad
of the S.C.G. Police Bureau. The Deputy Chief of the Special
Service Company is one Boo Feng-ming(蒲凤鸣), Chairman of the
Chung Nyi Association(忠义会). The address of the Investigation
Section is in the Tsing Ching Primary School(精勤小学), Pei
Nyien Li Alleyway(培凝里), Si Ling Road (西林路), outside the
West Gate, Tel No. 22889. I do not know where the Special
Service Corps Headquarters (Commander: Gen. Tsai Ching-chun,
Commissioner of Police Bureau) is located but presume it is at
the headquarters of the Police Bureau. The Investigation Section
has approximately thirty members and is commanded by one Yang
Foo-ling(楊福林). I know nothing further of the Section's
activities as they are kept from general knowledge. Further
I do not receive any pay for my services.

According to the instructions given to me by Liu Hwai, my
duties are to make enquiries about and report on the activities
of Japanese plainclothes men in the Settlement. I have also
been instructed to make when enquiries regarding Chinese traitors
and in cases there is sufficient evidence, I have been told, I
may call a polic to bring the traitors to the police station
to which the Special Service Company Headquarters will subsequently
make application for the handing over of the prisoner.

警方调查报告。

以下是傅多馬（Fu Tu-ma），定海人，由我 D. S. Larby 于1937年9月16日在警察总局录取，并由探员潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）翻译的供词：

我叫傅多馬（Fu Tu-ma），27岁，浙江定海人，原为新光小学（Sing Kwang Primary School）校长，现居住在 Chapel 区长兴路（Chang Shing Road）长兴里（Chang Shing Li Alleyway）的新光小学。

1937年8月20日，我加入了特别服务公司总部的调查科，该科由上海市警察局侦缉队队长刘槐（Liu Hwai）指挥。特别服务公司的副队长是忠义会（Chung Nyi Association）主席蒲凤鸣（Boo Feng-ming）。调查科的地址位于西门外西林路（Si Ling Road）培凝里（Pei Nyien Li Alleyway）的精勤小学（Tsing Ching Primary School），电话号码22889。我不知道特别服务队总部（指挥官：警察局局长蔡劲军将军 Gen. Tsai Ching-chun）位于何处，但推测其在警察局总部。调查科约有三十名成员，由杨福林（Yang Foo-ling）指挥。由于该科的活动对外保密，我对其活动一无所知。此外，我的服务没有任何报酬。

根据刘槐给我的指示，我的职责是调查并报告租界内日本便衣人员的活动。我还受命调查中国汉奸，据告知，在有充分证据的情况下，我可以叫警察将汉奸带到警察局，随后特别服务公司总部将申请移交囚犯。

    At about 4 p.m. to-day (16.9.37), I met a Chinese traitor
named Oong Tao-li(翁桃李) on Ferry Road near Mapai Road( I knew
him to be a traitor because a report to this effect had been
received by the Special Service Company ; I do not know, however,
whether the report was supported by any proof). Just as I was
about to call for the assistance of a policeman, one arrived on
the scene and brought Oong Tao-li to the Pootoo Road Police
Station. Since undertaking my present work, I have never
arrested any traitor in the Settlement, this, therefore, was
my first experience of such an occurence.
    The temporary pass for Chapei(translation attached) in
my possession was issued to me by Liu Hwai on September 8, 1937
at my request so that I might visit relatives residing in Chapei.

                                (Sd.) Fu Tu-ma

TRANSLATION.
No. 2043/S.

Shanghai, September 2, 1937.

A REPORT.
-----------

Subject: Organisation and activities of the
Shanghai Snipers' Corps.

Reference: Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai.

Chinese
The/snipers who have caused and are still causing
a lot of trouble to the Japanese, operate at the back
of their lines in Hongkew, Yangtsepoo, Woosung, etc.
and have been organised by General Tsai Ching Chun, Chief
of the Police Bureau of Greater Shanghai. They have been
recruited mainly from amongst unemployed workers, the
loafers, etc. Every sniper is provided by the Police
Bureau with a Mauser pistol or a rifle.

These "snipers" must not be confused with the Snipers'
Corps (上海別動隊總隊), which was organised at the beginning
of hostilities in Shanghai, with the assistance of citizens
who have had military training. This latter Corps has
for its purpose to assist the Police in maintaining peace
and order, to participate in the evacuation of refugees
and wounded soldiers, to locate and suppress "spies",
"traitors", smugglers, etc...

It is composed of three detachments (regiments),
3.000 strong each. Each detachment is divided into three
batallions. Each battalion is divided into five companies.
Each company is divided into five sections.

The organiser and present chief of the Corps is one
Tao Yi Sai (陶一珊), chief of military training of
Shanghai citizens. His headquarters is installed in the
Woosung Shanghai Garrison Commanders Headquarters in Lunghwa.

Only the first detachment (regiment) is armed. It is
page_data.zh:
译文。
编号 2043/S。

上海，1937年9月2日。

报告。
-----------

主题：上海狙击手队的组织与活动。

参考：上海中日敌对行动。

中文
给日本人造成且仍在造成许多麻烦的狙击手，在虹口、杨树浦、吴淞等地日军后方活动，由大上海警察局局长蔡劲军将军组织。他们主要从失业工人、游民等人群中招募。每位狙击手均由警察局配备一支毛瑟手枪或步枪。

这些“狙击手”不应与上海别动队总队混淆，后者是在上海战事初期，在有军事训练的市民协助下组织的。后者的目的是协助警察维持治安，参与难民和伤兵的疏散，定位并镇压“间谍”、“汉奸”、走私者等……

它由三个支队（团）组成，每支3,000人。每个支队分为三个营。每个营分为五个连。每个连分为五个排。

该队的组织者及现任队长为陶一珊，上海市民军事训练主任。其总部设在龙华的吴淞上海卫戍司令部总部内。

仅第一支队（团）配备武器。它是

page_data.en:
- 2 -

provided with old Mauser rifles. Its headquarters is in
Lunghwa. The men wear Khaki uniform and are in charge
of assisting the Police in maintaining peace and order in
Nantao, Lunghwa and the Western District of Shanghai (Hungjao
Road, Rubicon Road).

The headquarters of the 2nd detachment is installed
at Chemju. The men are not armed and wear a blue uniform.
They are in charge of assisting military and civil
authorities in the evacuation of refugees and wounded
soldiers.

The headquarters of the 3rd detachment is installed at
Sio Tung Men (East Gate), in the former offices of the
Police Bureau. The men do not wear any uniform. Their
duty is to locate spies and "traitors", to watch the
activities of smugglers, etc. They are divided in small
groups into the Concessions, to Nantao, Lunghwa and the
Western district of Shanghai.

Sd: Oussakovsky.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

配备旧式毛瑟步枪。其总部在龙华。队员身穿卡其色制服，负责协助警察在南市、龙华和上海西区（虹桥路、Rubicon Road（音译））维持治安。

第二支队总部设在 Chemju（音译）。队员未配备武器，身穿蓝色制服。他们负责协助军政当局疏散难民和伤兵。

第三支队总部设在小东门（东门），即前警察局办公室所在地。队员不穿制服。他们的职责是定位间谍和“汉奸”，监视走私者的活动等。他们分成小组分布在租界、南市、龙华和上海西区。

签名: Oussakovsky
